items.title: Oil prices fall despite Iran's ongoing attacks on tankers
items.summary: Despite Iran claiming daily attacks on takers around the Strait of Hormuz and escalating fighting between the Saudis and Iran's Houthi allies, oil prices continue to decline.

items.title: Iranian women praise singer lashed for not wearing a hijab
items.summary: Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed 74 times for the crime of "outraging public decency" after she live-streamed a concert without her hair covered.
items.t: Iranian women praise singer lashed for not wearing a hijab

items.title: Supermarket hostage situation in Colombia's Cartagena disrupts incoming flights
items.summary: Armed robbers took several people hostage at a supermarket in Colombia’s tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, prompting a major police operation and the temporary suspension of incoming flights, authorities said. Landings at Rafael Nunez airport resumed about 45 minutes later, after the military used a runway during the operation.
items.t: Supermarket hostage situation in Colombia's Cartagena disrupts incoming flights

items.title: Spacecraft enters Mercury's orbit after 8-year journey despite glitch
items.summary: BepiColombo was launched as a joint mission between the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency in October 2018.

items.t: Man on cruise ship goes overboard off Bahamas, search underway

items.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
items.summary: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.
items.t: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'

items.title: NATO allies anxious as war spreads beyond Ukraine, Russia borders
items.summary: As Ukraine attacks Russian ships in far-flung waters, some NATO nations are voicing increasing anxiety over the war's spread to new regions.
items.t: NATO allies anxious as war spreads beyond Ukraine, Russia borders

items.title: Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden
items.summary: Yemen's military on Tuesday said that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.
items.t: Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden

items.title: Cold case murder mystery solved 58 years after girl found dead
items.summary: Canadian police say they've solved a teen girl's mysterious murder case, nearly six decades after she was found dead.
items.t: Cold case murder mystery solved 58 years after girl found dead

items.title: New details emerge about U.S. involvement in drug lord's capture
items.summary: The U.S. has sought to line up allies across Latin America to allow U.S. forces to operate in their territories, with mixed responses from across the region.
items.t: New details emerge about U.S. involvement in drug lord's capture

items.title: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering
items.summary: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.
items.t: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering

items.title: 'We are ready to facilitate removal of Netanyahu': Head of Israel's Arab-majority Joint List
items.summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.
items.t: 'We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu' from power: Head of Israel's Joint List

items.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners
items.summary: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat. Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” in response to the decision.
items.t: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners

items.title: Irish plan offers Burnham breakthrough on Made in Europe
items.summary:
Irish presidency of EU proposes giving UK ‘partner’ status on assembly of cars in possible boost to reset of relations

  • Business live – latest updates

The UK would not have to follow the EU and apply tariffs on Chinese car imports under an Irish proposal that could prove another breakthrough for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, in his reset of relations with the bloc.

The proposal comes as the UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, told a parliamentary committee that there had been “a transformation in the EU view”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Irish plan offers Burnham breakthrough on Made in Europe

items.title: 'Tis the season to be green: Can the Christmas holidays be a present for the planet?
items.summary: With the holiday season just around the corner, we take a look at its environmental impact. We discuss how to make Christmas a little greener as consumers, whether plastic trees or natural ones are better for the planet, and what small steps we can all take to reduce our carbon footprint during the festivities.
items.t: 'Tis the season to be green: Can the Christmas holidays be a present for the planet?

items.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
items.summary:
Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

Continue reading...
items.t: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals

items.title: French police officer who shot teenager to face murder trial
items.summary: A French police officer will stand trial for murder in the killing of a teenager in 2023 that sparked violent protests across the country, the Versailles appeals court said on Tuesday. Nahel Merzouk, 17, was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car.
items.t: French police officer who shot teenager to face murder trial

items.title: Leaked data suggests 500,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine invasion
items.summary: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a huge dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. Two independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona say the death toll may rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.
items.t: Leaked data suggests 500,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine invasion

items.title: Burnham's EU reset brings back Brexit debate
items.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being "stuck in the past", as he trumpeted his EU reset deal on Monday. Burnham has in recent weeks smashed a consensus that Britain's acrimonious departure from the European Union was done and dusted, floating the possibility that Britain could apply to rejoin. Clovis Casali takes a closer look.
items.t: Burnham's EU reset brings back Brexit debate

items.title: 'Nina Roza' director: 'I was inspired by a real case of a child painter prodigy'
items.summary: The director of a film nominated by Canada for next year's Oscars has told FRANCE 24 she was inspired by stories of a child painter prodigy, as well as the idea of identity and what you leave behind when you change countries. The film "Nina Roza" tells the story of a Bulgarian man who leaves his homeland with his daughter and sets himself up as an art curator in Canada.
items.t: 'Nina Roza' director: 'I was inspired by a real case of a child painter prodigy'

items.title: UK’s Burnham on a mission to build public support EU reset
items.summary: While he insists it would be unthinkable to rejoin the bloc without another referendum, British PM Andy Burnham has nevertheless reopened the debate over Brexit. After striking a deal that brings the UK and the EU closer on issues including food export control standards, youth mobility and carbon emissions, he's set to discuss the future of the relationship with Brussels in the coming weeks and will present the results of the talks in December. It comes despite criticism from a host of former Conservative prime ministers.
items.t: UK’s Burnham on a mission to build public support EU reset

items.title: Prince William and Kate's country home broken into, 2 arrested
items.summary: Intruders have broken into the country residence of Prince William and Princess Catherine, British media reported Tuesday.
items.t: Prince William and Kate's country home broken into, 2 arrested

items.title: The French mayors refusing to back presidential candidates
items.summary: Tuesday marks the opening in Paris of the 108th Congress of French Mayors, where the presidential race is a contentious issue. Candidates need 500 mayor endorsements to run, yet nearly half of mayors this year say they refuse to endorse anyone. France 2 and Caitlin Brown have more.
items.t: The French mayors refusing to back presidential candidates

items.title: France's femicide orphans: The invisible victims of violence against women
items.summary: In France, 111 women were killed by their current or ex-partners in 2025 alone, leaving behind dozens of children. How can they rebuild their lives without their mother? How can they seek help? In this episode of France in Focus, we meet Cloé and Eva-Louise, whose world collapsed when their father brutally murdered their mother. FRANCE 24's Natacha Vesnitch, Olivia Bizot, Clément Di Roma and Aurore Cloé Dupuis report.
items.t: France's femicide orphans: The invisible victims of violence against women

items.title: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher after nude images sent to media
items.summary: Gisèle Pelicot, who spoke out about being drugged and raped by her husband and 50 other men, says she's been "once again humiliated."
items.t: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher after nude images sent to media

items.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
items.summary: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.
items.t: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?

items.summary: Pharmacies in Iran are closing, hospital deliveries have stalled and patients are rationing doses or turning to black markets.

Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

items.title: Chinese police contacted members of WeChat group after they discussed Melbourne vigil for HungryPanda rider
items.summary:
Several members of the group chat set up after the alleged murder of Feng Jianming say they or their parents were called by police from their home towns in China

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Chinese police have contacted several people who were part of a WeChat group that discussed attending a Melbourne vigil for Feng Jianming, the HungryPanda food delivery rider allegedly murdered earlier this month.

At least three members of the group set up after Feng’s death said they were contacted, raising concerns that Chinese authorities may have been alerted to discussions about the protest activity either automatically or manually by the Chinese-owned messaging and social app.

Continue reading...
items.t: Chinese police contacted members of WeChat group after they discussed Melbourne vigil for HungryPanda rider

items.title: Guardian Essential poll: Albanese’s disapproval rating hits highest level as problems mount for Labor
items.summary:
Australians also turn against AI datacentres, with nearly half saying they don’t want one near their home

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese’s approval ratings have nosedived in the latest Guardian Essential poll, with the prime minister reaching his highest level of disapproval after his net popularity plummeted 10 points in just a month.

Australians have also turned strongly against AI datacentres, with nearly half of the country saying they don’t want one near their home. Women, older people and One Nation and Greens supporters are among the most likely to reject living near a datacentre.

Continue reading...
items.t: Guardian Essential poll: Albanese’s disapproval rating hits highest level as problems mount for Labor

items.title: The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence
items.summary:
Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran

Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view.

Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geo-strategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race.

Continue reading...
items.t: The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence

items.title: Days out from the Victorian election, nine datacentre projects await approval. What will their fate be?
items.summary:
While parties have come out with policies on where datacentres can be built, not all are clear on whether they apply retrospectively

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Days out from the Victorian state election, the fate of nine datacentre projects remains uncertain, with some companies confident they will be able to get their projects across the line after Saturday.

There are nine datacentre projects currently awaiting approval according to the ministerial permits register, including the West Footscray expansion of NextDC’s M3 datacentre, which Guardian Australia reported has faced delays due to community blowback.

Continue reading...
items.t: Days out from the Victorian election, nine datacentre projects await approval. What will their fate be?

items.title: Rwanda's malaria cases on the rise: Climate change leads to more mosquitoes
items.summary: In Rwanda, malaria cases are on the rise due to climate change. Higher temperatures and prolonged rainfall are creating more breeding grounds for mosquitoes. According to researchers, the risk of infection could increase by as much as 20 percent by 2100 in the Rift Valley. Our correspondent Aurore Bayoud reports on Rwanda's efforts to tackle the problem.
items.t: Rwanda's malaria cases on the rise: Climate change leads to more mosquitoes

items.title: 'Political hunting ground': French presidential candidates campaign mayors' congress
items.summary: Candidates in next year’s French presidential election descended on the 108th Congress of French Mayors in Paris on Tuesday, hoping to win endorsements for their campaigns. France 24’s Luke Shrago reports.
items.t: 'Political hunting ground': French presidential candidates campaign mayors' congress

items.title: Trump's role in Huang's Nvidia return under scrutiny
items.summary: Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia was greeted with triumph by US President Donald Trump, and the AI chipmaker's stock price was sent soaring. But the national security implications of Huang's extra-marital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, as well as Trump's intervention in the operations of a company in which he holds stock, have stirred anger in Congress, with members from both parties vowing to investigate.
items.t: Trump's role in Huang's Nvidia return under scrutiny

items.title: In South Africa, parents' homemade sensory room helps children with ADHD
items.summary: Determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into an underwater-themed sensory room using recycled plastic bottles, cut-out flowers and ferns. Originally designed for children with conditions including ADHD and epilepsy, the space is now benefiting the wider community.
items.t: In South Africa, parents' homemade sensory room helps children with ADHD

items.title: DR Congo and Kenya agree to restore ties
items.summary: After years of strained relations over the conflict in eastern Congo, Kinshasa and Nairobi are moving towards a diplomatic reset. DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi met his Kenyan counterpart William Ruto over the weekend and they agreed to to restore normal ties and deepen economic and regional cooperation. Emmet Livingstone reports.
items.t: DR Congo and Kenya agree to restore ties

items.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six other people, medics say
items.summary: Israeli air strikes on the devastated Gaza Strip killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahel, director-general of the Palestinian territory's Internal Security Service on Tuesday, the ministry said. Another six people, including two police officers and a 17-year-old teenager, were killed in Israeli strikes across the enclave.
items.t: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six other people, medics say

items.title: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?
items.summary: A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.
items.t: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?

items.title: Advances in health and medicine: From space, ‘you discover things that are hidden' back on Earth
items.summary: When kids look up at the night sky and marvel at the moon and the stars, the mysteries of space can spark a sense of wonder and curiosity. One of France's most beloved astronauts, Thomas Pesquet, joins Eve Irvine to take us one step beyond with his new book, "Space in 100 Questions", offering space enthusiasts of all ages an otherworldly glimpse into the Final Frontier!
items.t: From space, ‘you discover things hidden' back on Earth: Advancing research in health and medicine

items.title: Leftwing coalition leader calls for rental revolution as Spain heads for snap election
items.summary:
Exclusive: Ada Colau hopes public anger over housing will transfer into support for her Broad Front coalition in Sunday’s vote

The leader of Spain’s leftwing Broad Front coalition has called for a drastic rethink of the country’s entire housing rental system, and described the eviction of an 87-year-old woman – the spark for nationwide protests that in turn triggered Sunday’s snap general election – as “the last straw” for desperate tenants.

“We’re not interested in small changes,” Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor, told the Guardian in an interview. “We want to reform the entire rental sector.”

Continue reading...
items.t: Leftwing coalition leader calls for rental revolution as Spain heads for snap election

items.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention
items.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, drawing approval/plaudits/cheers  from Wall Street and criticism from US lawmakers. The sudden reversal was the latest twist in the fallout from Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
items.t: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention

Georgina Long and subatomic physicist Anthony Thomas recognised in Prime Minister’s Prizes for Science

When Prof Georgina Long was starting out in melanoma treatment and research, “my waiting room would change so rapidly”.

Referring to her patients with stage 4 melanoma, the oncologist and medical director at the Melanoma Institute Australia said she wouldn’t “see the same face for more than nine months, 12 months maximum”.

items.title: EU to impose cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports next month
items.summary:
Temporary quotas on vehicles entering the bloc tariff-free will also apply to cars from the UK, Japan and Turkey

  • Business live – latest updates

The EU will next month impose its threatened caps on the number of Chinese hybrid cars that can be imported into the bloc without facing a tariff, the European Commission has announced.

The quotas will also apply to hybrids from Japan, Turkey, South Korea and the UK, but the principal purpose is to limit imports from China after an agreement with Beijing in October that has led to a rise in exports to the bloc.

items.summary: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

items.summary: Pope Francis suffered a profound spiritual crisis in 2021-2022 linked to temptations to exercise power omnipotently, his diary reveals, adding that he overcame it by entrusting himself entirely to God's mercy.

items.title: Social media companies could be fined 5% of global revenue after Labor and Greens join forces on online safety laws
items.summary:
Individual Australians will be able to sue big tech firms for harm suffered online under compromise deal

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Big tech companies may face “multibillion-dollar” fines and individuals could sue social media companies in court under Australia’s new digital duty of care laws, with the Greens to support the bill’s passage after extracting major amendments from Labor.

From late 2027, Australians will also be able opt out of addictive online algorithms under the new legislation, while the “endless scroll” of social media feeds may also cease.
items.t: Social media companies could be fined 5% of global revenue after Labor and Greens join forces on online safety laws

items.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
items.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

items.title: Malaysia to send thousands of migrants back to Myanmar as PM acknowledges junta’s ‘atrocities’
items.summary:
Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement comes days after the ICJ found Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya minority

Malaysia says it will send thousands of migrants and refugees back to Myanmar, despite acknowledging that many asylum seekers in the country had been victims of “atrocities” carried ​out by the junta in Naypyidaw.

The announcement comes just days after the UN’s highest court ruled Myanmar had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.

items.title: Ebikes, screens and failing manners pose challenge for Dutch cycling culture
items.summary:
Awareness campaign reminds public ‘traffic is a team sport’ amid less civility and more collisions on roads

For decades the Netherlands has been famed for its proud cycling culture, with a network of 23,000 miles of bike paths used by everyone from children under eight to adults over 80.

In recent years, however, like so many countries around the world, it has seen a dramatic change in the type of vehicles using those lanes: no longer the preserve of pedal bikes, they are used by all manner of two-wheeled vehicles including electric cargo bikes, thick-tyred “fatbikes”, speed pedelecs, electric scooters and even some micro cars.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ebikes, screens and failing manners pose challenge for Dutch cycling culture

items.title: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter after Russian military aircraft approach

The order was issued after aircraft entered the country’s air defence identification zone over the island of Ulleungdo

Residents of a remote South Korean island were ordered to take shelter on Tuesday morning after several Russian military aircraft came close to entering its airspace, prompting a pre-emptive alert from the military that anticipated a violation.

The defence ministry said it would summon the Russian defence attaché on Tuesday afternoon to lodge a strong protest.

items.t: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter after Russian military aircraft approach

items.title: China sentences official to death for spying for foreign country

Accused official leaked national secrets to unnamed country and received payments worth over $150,000, state-linked publisher says

A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for spying for a foreign country, a government-linked publisher has said.

Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, said the convicted person was surnamed Ma and was approached and recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while working abroad.

items.title: Butt of the joke: Trump impersonator mocks president at Canada press dinner
items.summary:
Carney watches on as comedian lampoons US leader and his interest in men’s backsides at correspondents’ event Ottawa

Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday.

With coiffed hair and an ill-fitting suit, comedian Mark Critch – who portrays the president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes – danced on to the stage and lampooned the trade war Trump started as well as the president’s threats to annex Canada.

British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
items.t: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
